title: Impulse and momentum with calculus
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: NEW-momentum-calc-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; NEW-momentum-calc-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; NEW-momentum-calc-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; NEW-momentum-calc-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: NEW-momentum-calc-1#N.3, NEW-momentum-calc-1#N.5, NEW-momentum-calc-1#N.7, NEW-momentum-calc-1#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Momentum
items.clue: Quantity p = mv; its rate of change with time equals the net force.

items.label: Impulse
items.clue: Integral of the net force over time: the area under a force–time graph.

items.label: Average force
items.clue: Total area under the F–t graph divided by the time interval; 8.0 N for the puck.

items.label: Newton's second law
items.clue: States that the net force on a body equals dp/dt, which reduces to ma when m is constant.

questions.stem: The net force on an object moving along the x-axis is F(t) = 3.0 + 6.0t², where F is in newtons and t is in seconds. What is the impulse delivered to the object from t = 0 to t = 2.0 s?

A cart moving in the +x direction is slowed by a resistive force, and its momentum is p(t) = p₀e^(−t/τ), where p₀ and τ are positive constants and t is time. What is the magnitude of the net force on the cart at the instant its momentum is p₀/2?
For which of the following systems does F_net = ma, where m is the mass of the system and a is its acceleration, give an incorrect value for the net external force on the system?

options.text: A satellite moving at constant speed in a circular orbit around the Earth
An open railcar rolling at constant velocity while rain falls vertically into it
A ball thrown straight upward, at the instant it reaches its highest point
A car moving at constant velocity along a level road while its engine is running

questions.explanation: The railcar's mass grows while its velocity stays constant, so a = 0, but dp/dt = (dm/dt)v is not zero: a horizontal force must give each new drop the car's velocity. F_net = ma holds only for constant mass.

questions.stem: A hose sends water horizontally at 2.0 kg s⁻¹ and 15 m s⁻¹ against a vertical wall. The water stops at the wall and runs straight down it. What is the magnitude of the horizontal force the water exerts on the wall? Use g = 10 m s⁻².
questions.explanation: F = v dm/dt = (15 m s⁻¹)(2.0 kg s⁻¹) = 30 N. Each second the wall takes 30 kg m s⁻¹ of horizontal momentum from the water, so the water pushes on the wall with 30 N.
